subject: URGENT: EdgeCore private cluster — sudden p95 tail latency & increased 504s
messages:
From: ops@edgecore.ai
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: julia.singh@edgecore.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T08:17:00Z
Subject: Production: sudden tail latency and 504s on private cluster

Hi Evelyn,

Heads-up — since ~06:00 UTC this morning we've observed a sustained jump in p95/p99 latency and an uptick in 504s from our private Redwood cluster in us-west-2. Our app surface that does short-text classification is showing intermittent token-generation stalls: requests that normally finish under 120ms are now frequently hitting 800ms–2s, and a small percentage convert to 504s.

What we've checked so far:
- No increase in QPS vs baseline (within 3% of expected).
- Pod/worker CPU is fine; GPU utilization is steady but occasional NVLINK timeouts reported in host logs.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~92% yesterday to ~47% (attached kvcache-lookup-stats-20270611.csv).
- We captured runtime logs and a heap profile (attached).

This started shortly after a routine agent update (redwood-runtime v1.8.4) that was pushed at 02:30 UTC. Rolling back to v1.8.3 on one node reduced tail latency immediately for that node.

We're treating this as P1 — customers are seeing latency regressions that affect SLAs. Can you confirm whether Redwood has any known regressions in the v1.8.4 runtime related to KV cache eviction or kernel selection? We can schedule a maintenance window but given business impact we need an exec-level sync if rollback or a config remediation is required.

Attachments: redwood_runtime_logs_20270611.zip, kvcache-lookup-stats-20270611.csv, heap-profile-20270612.txt

Thanks,
Samir Patel
SRE, EdgeCore Inc
ops@edgecore.ai


From: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
To: ops@edgecore.ai
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T08:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden tail latency and 504s on private cluster

Samir — thanks for the quick signal and the attachments.

Short answer: we saw a surfaced issue in an internal test farm after v1.8.4, but it wasn't flagged as P1 because it only reproduced under heavy prefix-KV churn. Given your rollback note and the immediate improvement on the one node, we want to treat this as a production regression and get an emergency playbook running.

Immediate next steps (we'll own coordination):
- We will open an internal incident and run a targeted rollback on a canary subset of your pool. If rollback mirrors your revert, we will schedule a full rollback with a two-hour maintenance window (target: 12:00–14:00 UTC).
- Engineering will investigate root cause: possible KV-cache indexer mis-shard + new kernel selection path in v1.8.4. Markus will lead the kernel/quant path triage; Irene will handle orchestration + rollback.
- Please share the job ids and the exact model variants hitting 504s (if you have them).

I'll escalate to the on-call product & infra leads now and we will set an exec sync in 90 minutes. If you're open to it, please keep one rollback-capable node in a steady state for comparison.

—Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability (Redwood Inference)
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai

Subject: Exec brief: EdgeCore private cluster — regression tied to v1.8.4 runtime (P1)

Executive summary:
- Impact: EdgeCore (large account, RDW-4721) experiencing elevated tail latency and intermittent 504s on a private VPC deployment after runtime update v1.8.4; rollback to v1.8.3 on one node reproduced improvement. Customer-facing impact on short-text classification endpoints; potential SLA exposure.
- Scope: us-west-2 private pool (estimated 18 nodes, multi-tenant within EdgeCore's reserved cluster).
- Immediate mitigation: partial rollback scheduled (canary completed at 10:30 UTC showed p95 drop ~60%). Full rollback proposed 12:00–14:00 UTC pending approval.
- Root hypothesis: v1.8.4 introduced a kernel-selection change that interacts poorly with our new KV cache eviction heuristic causing cache thrashing under certain sequence-length distributions.
- Customer asks: rapid remediation + post-mortem, and potential SLA credit if full rollback isn't completed within the proposed window.

Proposed asks from leadership:
1) Approve full rollback now to stem customer impact (engineering to manage migration plan).
2) If rollback is not feasible in next 80 minutes, authorize an exec-sync with EdgeCore to explain next steps and offer temporary SLA relief.
3) Prioritize a short-term release (v1.8.5-urgent) to harden KV cache eviction and revert kernel-selection path.

Data: logs and kvcache stats attached; ticket created: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/47321.

Irene will coordinate the rollback and will keep the execs updated; Markus will prepare a hotfix branch and a test matrix.

—Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Exec brief: EdgeCore private cluster — regression tied to v1.8.4 runtime (P1)

Quick technical update from triage:
- Confirmed reproduction locally with a synthetic load that mirrors EdgeCore's prefix churn. The new kernel path in v1.8.4 defers some KV cache lookups in favor of speculative kernel prefetch; under high churn this increases cache-miss amplification.
- Temporary mitigations validated:
  * revert kernel-selection flag (--use-speculative-kernel=false) => immediate p95 improvement.
  * reduce KV eviction aggressiveness (patch attached: proposed-kvcache-patch.diff) => raises hit-rate back toward baseline in 10–15m for steady traffic.
  * we saw one NVLINK timeout in logs; working with infra to validate hardware link health but that appears orthogonal.
- Plan: 1) push a controlled rollback to v1.8.3 across the cluster (IR will schedule and own ops), 2) prepare v1.8.5-urgent with the kvcache tweak + kernel flag guard, 3) run post-rollback validation and a special test harness to prevent future regression.

Attachments included: proposed-kvcache-patch.diff, kvcache-lookup-stats-20270611.csv (sanitized), heap-profile-20270612.txt

I'll join the 12:00 UTC call and bring a short slide deck with before/after perf plots.

—Markus Klein
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
